slides.say: An isosceles triangle A B C is inscribed in a circle with center O, and A B equals A C. Given: angle B A C is fifty-six degrees. What is angle A B O?
Angle A B O is the angle marked x, at B, between B A and the radius B O. [short pause] There are two ways to solve this, a math way and a shorter psychometric way. Let's start with the math.
at: Angle A B O is the angle marked x

slides.say: Angle B A C is an inscribed angle, and it intercepts the arc B C. Angle B O C is a central angle, and it intercepts the same arc.
at: it intercepts the arc B C

slides.say: Remember, a central angle is twice the inscribed angle on the same arc. So angle B O C is two times fifty-six, which is one hundred twelve.
at: So angle B O C is two times

slides.say: Now look at triangle B O C. O B and O C are both radii, so they're equal, and the triangle is isosceles. This time the top angle is one hundred twelve, not sixty, so it isn't equilateral.
at: Now look at triangle B O C

slides.say: The two base angles share one hundred eighty minus one hundred twelve, which is sixty-eight. Half of sixty-eight is thirty-four. So angle O B C is thirty-four, and so is angle O C B.
Careful, thirty-four is angle O B C, not our x. It's choice number two, and it's a trap if you stop here.
[pause] Now let's use the given we haven't used yet. A B equals A C, so triangle A B C is isosceles, and its base angles, at B and at C, are equal.
at: A B equals A C, so triangle

slides.say: The top angle is fifty-six. So the angles at B and C share one hundred eighty minus fifty-six, which is one hundred twenty-four. Half of one hundred twenty-four is sixty-two. So the whole angle A B C is sixty-two.

The whole angle at B is sixty-two, and its lower part, O B C, is thirty-four. So x is what's left, sixty-two minus thirty-four, which is twenty-eight. Choice number one is our answer. Notice that sixty-two, choice number three, is the whole angle, not x.
at: Choice number one is our answer

slides.say: [pause] The math solution was quite short. Now the psychometric solution. It uses symmetry and a helper line.
From the center O, let's draw a radius to the vertex A.

Triangle A B C is isosceles, and an isosceles triangle is symmetric. So the radius O A cuts the angle at A into two equal parts. Fifty-six divided by two is twenty-eight, so we get twenty-eight and twenty-eight.

slides: We don't need to prove it. This isn't a school math exam. It's an easy question early in the section, and none of the choices says the answer can't be found. So we can trust the symmetry.

slides.say: Now look at triangle A O B. O A and O B are both radii, so it's isosceles too, and its base angles are equal. So x equals angle O A B, which is twenty-eight. Choice number one again. This way is shorter, with fewer calculations. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: Now look at triangle A O B
So x equals angle O A B
